title: Website Opportunities shared research: one place per restaurant shared by every account, one place job, Tracy's cost ledger with caps, backfill of per-account research into places (with a one-time Google website pass that shares what the account already collected), URL to Google merge with an operator queue, /ops/wo Places doors, and WO_SHARED_RESEARCH=off falling back to the per-account path
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout (dependencies installed, TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a scratch Postgres) run the server test files named in run.cmd.
S2: Read the pass/fail counts and the tests named below.
expect: Two accounts that save the same Google place get one place job and the same published snapshot; one account's cancel stops only its own request.
A client's candidate never becomes a source of the shared place; an account's private pages stay its own overlay, including the PageSpeed of its own website.
Paid calls of a place run are reserved in Tracy's ledger and pause the job at the cap; an account may create only newPlacesPerAccountPerDay new places a day.
WO_SHARED_RESEARCH=0 runs the per-account research and claims no place job.
The backfill links every opportunity, publishes one snapshot from the newest research, copies pictures to places/<place>/ keeping old keys, resumes after failed copies, and a re-run changes nothing.

The backfill's website pass asks Google for websiteUri once per place, charged once in the ledger (a re-run asks and charges nothing); over the cap the place waits and a later pass finishes it; no Google key asks nothing; the website is verified only when it is the one the account collected and socials only from that website's crawl; a new snapshot shares their pictures under places/<place>/ while a brief keeps its old snapshot; a place its own research published is left alone.
A pasted URL that redirects to Google's website merges into the Google place; a busy place makes the merge wait; ambiguous pairs wait for an operator; merge then split restores exactly.

/ops/wo Places lists places with accounts, costs, freshness and media; only an owner or admin from the same origin can act; the merge queue shows pending pairs and approved merges still waiting or failed.
